selectedOriginals.inspection: Full actual 2025 southeast aerial inspected: entire connected castle and open courtyard, four cylindrical keep corners and four steep pavilion roofs, central lantern, chapel/royal wings and two taller outer end towers, three low enclosure ranges and two flat terrace-roofed front towers. Six restored open roof lanterns have current blue-grey lead/metal finishes. Moats and gardens control orientation but are not building geometry. Cars/people/landscape excluded.

additionalInspected.caption: Roof of the Château de Chambord with its numerous towers
additionalInspected.inspection: Full 2007 roof original inspected: large open central lantern and high ornate stair turrets, squared tall chimneys with circle/diamond inlays, crossed mullioned dormers, four-cone village silhouette, steep slate roofs, open roof balustrades and corbelled cornice. Pre-2023 restrained lantern finish is historical, not the current finish control. Literal salamanders/heraldic figures are not copied.

additionalInspected.caption: Northwest façade of Chambord castle. Built between 1519 and 1547 by François I, it was heavily extended afterwards by Henri II and Louis XIV to its final shape we know well today. Chambord castle is an example of Renaissance architecture. It is also the largest castle of the Loire valley, measuring 156m long and topping 56m height. A UNESCO world heritage site since 1981.
additionalInspected.inspection: Full 2012 northwest facade panorama inspected: garden-facing keep with three body levels, four great round keep towers, tall outer end towers, lower connecting galleries with round ground arcades and tall crossed glazing, side-wing steep roofs/dormers, repeated horizontal body mouldings and vertical pilaster grid. Moat/garden retaining walls and detached service houses excluded. Pre-restoration roof caps differ from current 2025 aerial.

additionalInspected.caption: Les châteaux de la Loire.
additionalInspected.inspection: Full 2013 entrance original inspected: low enclosure facade has real arched courtyard portal, broad pilasters and triangular stone pediment, tall divided windows and an open roof balustrade. Keep appears behind the low roof; central lantern, tall chimney stacks and four roof towers remain individually distinct. Visitors, flag cloth and lighting decoration omitted.

additionalInspected.caption: Les châteaux de la Loire.
additionalInspected.inspection: Full 2013 courtyard keep original inspected: three storeys, tall mullioned window groups, small intermediate lights, square pilasters and moulded horizontal bands. Two upper left bays form actual recessed open round-headed galleries, distinct from adjoining arched glazed windows. Raised threshold/steps at ground and turned terrace balustrade.

additionalInspected.caption: Les châteaux de la Loire.
additionalInspected.inspection: Full 2013 royal-wing original inspected: court-facing wing has divided windows and large dormers; projecting circular open stair tower with round arched openings, paired columns, curved/raked stair parapets and a shallow dome. Round/diamond slate inlays on stone and decorative cornices. Unseen stair engineering remains proportional.

additionalInspected.caption: Les châteaux de la Loire.
additionalInspected.inspection: Full 2013 low inner-range original inspected: long single-storey enclosure wall has tall cross-mullioned windows, carved pilasters, cornice brackets and actual turned roof balustrade. Low range joins round flat-roofed front towers. Keep cornices, conical roofs, tall decorated chimneys and upper gallery arches corroborated.

additionalInspected.caption: Les châteaux de la Loire.
additionalInspected.inspection: Full 2013 roof-detail original inspected: round and diamond dark inlays, divided dormer sash, open parapet balusters, decorated tall stack and small stair turret. Original simplified scroll/rosette geometry may capture density; literal carved royal beasts, monograms, coats of arms and inscriptions are excluded.

sources.inspection: Owner account read: square keep with four corner towers, two later lateral wings/court enclosure, centered Greek-cross arrangement and central double stair. Facades use horizontal mouldings and vertical pilasters; upper skyline is dense with chimneys and stair turrets. Interior helix reconstruction is outside scope.

Owner terrace description read: central lantern is the highest point at56m. Roof pavilion skyline contains stair turrets, chimneys and dormers; upper carving is distinct from restrained lower facades.

Owner restoration record read: six roof lanterns restored2021–June2023; four keep lanterns in lead and two outer lanterns in slate. Nominal lantern height12m with vane,10.3m without. Current restored lead ornament/gilding differs from pre2023 photos; use the2025 aerial for current finish.

Both current owner-plan pages visually inspected. PDF metadata datedJanuary2025 despite2022 URL. Confirms connected keep, chapel/royal wings and court enclosure, terrace roof plan,156m nominal main frontage and56m highest point. Floor plans are visitor diagrams, not measured construction drawings.

Official API documentation already read for the same service. Six sequential4500-point-or-smaller requests preserve exact provider responses; effective source resolution and surveyed accuracy remain unspecified.
IGN primary open-data policy read; public geographic data distributed under Etalab2.0, with attribution retained.

scope: Main keep, four cylindrical corner towers, outer wings and distinctive roof lantern/chimney skyline; exclude distant park structures.
limitations: Eight local originals individually inspected and all40 candidate contact views reviewed. Historical facade/plan engravings, interiors, Quebec, Montsoreau, Schwerin, Waddesdon and Zamosc do not control the current Chambord exterior.

Main connected château, keep/four drums, chapel/royal wings and two tall outer towers, low court enclosure/two flat front towers, current roof skyline and immediate thresholds only. Moats, formal gardens, bridges in the park, detached service buildings, interiors, trees, people, cars and flag cloth excluded.

Current2025 aerial controls overall massing and restored lantern finish. Earlier2007–2013 photos control visible stone/window details, not current lead polychromy or gilding. Original simplified abstract carving only, no literal heraldry or inscriptions.

Nominal156m frontage and56m central lantern height are owner controls. Native connected outline is approximately157.1×112.5m; preserve it rather than forcing a nominal bounding rectangle. Other heights and fine dimensions are map/photo estimates, not surveys.

Acquire and independently verify unchanged terrain before authoring. Do not flatten/fill host ground to match the castle. Native part heights are general massing evidence; courtyard void, open galleries, entrance portal, exterior stair arches and roof lanterns require actual negative space at appropriate levels.

Independent official IGN ground is used for the bounded site review. Original Terrarium baseline retains substantial building/site returns and is preserved as rejected evidence. Hosts need a compatible ground field; default coarse-ground compatibility is not certified.
